articles.title: Why Utah nabbed undersized DT Jireh Moe from the transfer portal when other teams ‘shied away’
articles.summary: A lot of teams ‘shied away’ from ‘undersized’ DT Jireh Moe in transfer portal. Utah didn’t, and now Moe is breaking out in a young Ute defensive tackles room...
articles.body:
On paper, Jireh Moe doesn't look like your prototypical college football defensive tackle.

Moe is officially listed on Utah's roster at 6-foot, though head coach Morgan Scalley admits that he's actually shorter than that, and at 280 pounds, he's a good 20-plus pounds lighter than most of his teammates in his position room.

Moe's measurables, along with the fact that he previously played at bottom-dwelling Group of Six school San Jose State , perhaps caused some coaches to skip over him when he entered the transfer portal after the 2025 season.

Scalley and his coaching staff, however, turned on the tape and liked what they saw.

Moe's one-on-one reps against Power Four competition especially stood out to Scalley and the Utes' recruiting team, leading them to believe he would be able to excel when facing that level of team nearly every week while at Utah.

In fact, Scalley said the Utes' analytics showed that Moe was one of the best defensive tackles available in the transfer portal. 247Sports ranked him as the No. 97 defensive lineman in the 2026 portal, while On3 had him as the No. 293 defensive lineman.

Utah's staff seeing something not many other people did has been a hallmark of Scalley's going back to his time recruiting underrated defensive players such as Devin Lloyd , a two-star prospect in high school who is now one of the NFL's best linebackers.

With Moe, the measureables didn't matter nearly as much as the talent that was evident while he was at San Jose State.

"What we saw on film is he's a football player," Scalley said. "He's a football player and you saw him going up against really good competition, and again, you always look for those one-on-one matchups. When they're in a one-on-one situation, are they winning?

"Our analytics said that he was the best in the pool of anyone, but people, because of his size, a lot of people shied away from him. We did not, because again, he showed it versus powerful teams. I don't know of many that have a better personality."

Moe never started in his freshman season at San Jose State in 2025, but quickly grew into a dependable rotation option. He gained the trust of the coaching staff, making his debut at No. 6 Texas , where he graded out as one of the Spartans' best defensive players in the game after registering two tackles and a quarterback hurry.

Against Stanford , Moe was once against one of the best defenders for San Jose State. Those two games, plus a season stat line of 28 tackles, two tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and a team-high PFF season grade of 83.1 suggested that Moe was ready to make the leap to the next level of college football.

All offseason long, Ute coaches talked up Moe, with defensive tackles coach Luther Elliss saying during fall camp that Moe has been one of the most consistent players since spring ball.

"He understands that he has to be a technician, and he's very good, if not one of our best technicians day in and day out, so I think that really helps him," Elliss said. "He is strong and explosive. He's very explosive and he has some really good things."

While Moe has to be more of a technician than some other defensive tackles who can overwhelm offensive linemen with their size, developing that deep skill set has been what has allowed him to rise to the top of Utah's depth chart.

And a certain height and size isn't required to be great, as Ellliss, who played 10 seasons at defensive tackle in the NFL, reminds us.

"Just start looking at John Randle, Warren Sapp, Aaron Donald . You look at all those guys, some of the greatest ones here recently are around that six-foot mark, 280-ish, 300 maybe," Elliss said.

"To me, size, the measureables are what they are — measureables. At the end of the day, it's about can you play this game, and (Moe) can play this game."

Though he started in the Utes' season-opener against Idaho , Moe played just 14 snaps and did not register a tackle. Ute coaches opted to save him for the bigger game against Arkansas and test out some of the depth players at defensive tackle.

Moe was rested and ready to go against Arkansas and turned in a dominant performance.

He was graded Utah's best-performing defensive player with a PFF grade of 85.7 and notched a sack, a team-high two tackles for loss and a quarterback hurry to go alongside eight tackles.

"Jireh Moe, eight tackles, two TFLs, one sack — all over the place," Scalley said. "He didn't show up on the stat sheet Game 1. Sometimes that happens, but the biggest reason we took that guy in the portal was because of the one-on-one matchups that he would consistently win, and that guy is so active. Impressive game from him tonight."

Moe's most impressive play of the game was on his sack of Arkansas quarterback KJ Jackson as he unleashed a spin move to easily get by Razorback offensive lineman Kobe Branham and stick Jackson.

"Just playing fast and just trusting my coaches too on play calls and all that, just putting us in the right spot," Moe said.

Though there's still a long way to go in the 2026 season, Saturday's performance by Moe and fellow starter Karson Kaufusi answered some of the preseason questions surrounding the Utes' young defensive tackles group.

The Utes held Razorbacks to just 2.2 yards per rush and made life difficult for Jackson throughout the game, sacking him four times, forcing seven quarterback hurries and batting passes down at the line of scrimmage.

"Me and Kars, I'm blessed to have him on my side," Moe said. "Kars, he's a very lengthy guy. He's a technician, too. He's a really good player, a really smart player, too. He helped me be who I am today too, technique-wise and getting smarter and getting in my playbook, but I believe we complement each other."

While Utah's defensive line will face greater challenges than a below-standard Arkansas offensive line this season, the Hogs still had a lot of size, and the Utes aced its first test.

"If you look at any SEC team that you go against, it's impressive size. At our press conference on Monday, I said, the tale of tape's going to be the offensive line, defensive line and I was so proud of them," Scalley said.

articles.title: Thoughts on a 7-6 Rangers win
articles.body:
And the Rangers win their first road series since June 29-July 1 in Cleveland !

That was also a little more exciting that I'd have preferred.

It did feel like from the outset that the Rangers were going to have success in this game. A line drive single by Justin Foscue to start things off, followed the second-longest home run of Corey Seager 's career, will do that.

Statcast had the Seager homer at 458 feet. Only once in his career — back in 2021, with the Dodgers — has Seager hit the ball farther.

Its also tied with Bryce Eldridge for the 28th longest home run hit this season in the majors.

Its the third longest home run hit at Chase Field this season.

Its the longest home run hit by a Ranger this year. Jake Burger 's 447 foot shot against the Tigers on July 5 was the previous high.

Gabriel Moreno homered off of Cal Quantrill to lead off the fourth, making it a 2-1 game, but then the Rangers capitalized on clownball in the top of the fifth to make it a comfy game.

Justin Foscue reached on an E5 by Nolan Arenado , on a ball that took a bad hope. A line drive Corey Seager single was followed by a Josh Jung single that Lars Nootbar…well…

If you don't want to watch the video, Jung looped it into left field, where Nootbar was coming in for it. He pulled up, realizing in couldn't make the catch, but then had the ball bounce between his legs and behind him, allowing both Foscue and Seager to score. Brandon Nimmo later blooped a two out single into no man's land to bring home Jung, and Texas was up 5-1.

Two more came across the next inning, with Danny Jansen doubling home Ezequiel Duran , Evan Carter pinch hitting for Foscue and smoking it but right at Jordan Lawlar in center, then Seager drilling a single to bring home Jansen.

Seager even advanced to second on the throw, leading Dave Raymond and Mike Bascik to comment on how good, physically, Seager is feeling. Feeling good Corey Seager is a good thing.

Because I'm feeling good about this game and this win, we will not talk about the relievers, other than to note that Robert Garcia did good work in the eighth in the second of back-to-back outings, a good sign, given both how long he was on the injured list as well as how badly the Rangers need quality relief options right now.

Quantrill had thrown just 65 pitches through six, and there seemed to be some question as to whether he'd come back out for the seventh, despite the low pitch count. Quantrill did come out, though he was pulled after allowing a Geraldo Perdomo single.

Post-game, it was reported Quantrill was dealing with back tightness, which is why he didn't go longer.

Meanwhile, the Astros of Houston lost, putting the Rangers two games back in the American League West, though really three, since the Astros have the tiebreaker. The Guardians won, meaning the Rangers are two back in the Wild Card, and the Blue Jays won, which means the Jays are still a game ahead of Texas among the teams chasing the Guardians. Fortunately, Texas has the tiebreaker advantage against both Cleveland and Toronto .

Toronto, I will note, plays three games in Arlington Friday through Sunday, with Cleveland no doubt hoping neither team splits.

Before Toronto is Boston . On the plus side, the Rangers are facing Boston at the Shed. On the minus side, Boston is 82-68 this season, with the third best record in the American League. On the plus side, they are eight and a half back in the division, four and a half back for the first Wild Card spot, and six games up on Cleveland for the third Wild Card spot, so while they are not going to be treating the games like exhibitions, their postseason berth and seeding seems pretty well sewn up.

Cal Quantrill touched 95.7 mph with his fastball, averaging 94.2 mph, and 95.9 mph with his sinker, averaging 94.0 mph. Tyler Alexander 's fastball reached 93.9 mph. Robert Garcia topped out at 94.7 mph with his fastball. Jacob Latz 's fastball maxed out at 96.8 mph.

Corey Seager's had a 110.3 mph home run, a 106.3 mph single, and a 105.8 mph single. Elias Diaz had a 109.6 mph line out. Evan Carter had a 105.8 mph fly out. Danny Jansen had a 104.4 mph double. Brandon Nimmo had a 102.5 mph single.

Now an off day before starting a nine game homestand. Let's spend the next 48 hours enjoying the win.

images.caption: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jacob Latz #67 of the Texas Rangers celebrates a 7-6 win against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on September 13, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images

articles.title: 2026 Série D final draws crowd of 36,500
articles.summary: Parque do Sabiá, in Uberlândia, welcomed around 36,500 fans for the second leg of the 2026 Série D final between Uberlândia and ASACredits: Rafael Ribeiro/CB...
articles.body:
Parque do Sabiá, in Uberlândia, welcomed around 36,500 fans for the second leg of the 2026 Série D final between Uberlândia and ASA Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

The Série D final between Uberlândia and ASA drew 36,500 fans this Sunday (13) and featured a great celebration in the stands. At Parque do Sabiá, a packed stadium witnessed Uberlândia's title over ASA, secured with a 2-0 win in Arapiraca (AL) and a 1-1 draw at home, as well as the champions' celebrations.

In 2025, Santa Cruz hosted the first match to decide the winner. Arena de Pernambuco, in São Lourenço da Mata (PE), welcomed 45,500 people. Despite the support, Barra-SC won 2-1 and then claimed the title with a goalless draw in Itajaí (SC).

In the 2019 edition, nearly 45,000 people watched Manaus x Brusque at Arena da Amazônia, in Manaus. The Amazonas and Santa Catarina sides drew 2-2 across the two matches, and Brusque took the title on penalties by a score of 6-5.

Parque do Sabiá, in Uberlândia, welcomed 36,500 fans for the second leg of the 2026 Série D final between Uberlândia and ASA Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

Four years earlier, Albertão Stadium in Teresina had its stands filled by more than 40,000 people. On that occasion, River-PI was chasing the title against Botafogo-SP, but finished as runner-up after a goalless draw and failing to overturn the 3-2 loss in the first leg in Ribeirão Preto (SP).

In 2012, Sampaio Corrêa won Série D in front of more than 40,000 fans at Castelão, in São Luís, with a 2-0 victory over CRAC-GO. In the first match, in Catalão (GO).

Finally, in 2011, around 55,000 passionate Santa Cruz supporters backed the Cobra Coral in the final. Despite the fans' efforts, Tupi-MG were crowned champions, with another victory over the Pernambuco side, this time by 2-0 — the Minas Gerais team had come in off a 1-0 win.

With 44 years of history, the biggest venue in the interior of the state of Minas Gerais is located in the eastern area of the city of Uberlândia, the second most populous in Minas Gerais, with more than 710,000 inhabitants, according to the 2022 IBGE census — Belo Horizonte ranks first, with around 2.3 million.

Parque do Sabiá was inaugurated on May 27, 1982, the date it hosted Brazil 's 7-0 rout of Ireland — Sócrates (2), Serginho (2), Falcão , Luizinho and Zico all found the net. Besides marking the official opening, the match also set the stadium's attendance record: 72,733 spectators.

The venue also hosted a goalless draw between Brazil and Paraguay in the Copa América on October 20, 1983. Four years later, on December 9, Valdo and Renato secured a come-from-behind 2-1 win over Chile. Then, on May 28, 1991, the Seleção beat Bulgaria 3-0 in a friendly, with two goals from Neto and one from João Paulo.

Parque do Sabiá, in Uberlândia, welcomed around 40,000 fans for the second leg of the 2026 Série D final between Uberlândia and ASA Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

images.caption: 2026 Série D final draws crowd of 36,500

articles.title: Payton Tolle starts with immaculate inning, Roman Anthony gets key hit as Red Sox beat Royals 4-1
articles.summary: Payton Tolle opened the game with an immaculate inning, Roman Anthony hit a go-ahead single and the Boston Red Sox beat the Kansas City Royals 4-1 on Sunday...
articles.body:
BOSTON (AP) — Payton Tolle opened the game with an immaculate inning , Roman Anthony hit a go-ahead single and the Boston Red Sox beat the Kansas City Royals 4-1 on Sunday in a game that's start was delayed by rain.

Tolle is the first Boston pitcher to throw an immaculate inning (three strikeouts on nine pitches) to start a game since Hall of Famer Pedro Martinez did it on May 18, 2002.

Caleb Durbin hit a solo homer and Trevor Story added a game-breaking two-run single for the Red Sox, who took the final two games of the three-game series.

Carter Jensen drove in the Royals' run with a pinch-hit single. Kansas City was looking for its first series win in Boston since 2017.

In the seventh, Anthony lined an opposite-field single against reliever Connor Thomas after Craig Kimbrel (1-5) walked the first two batters.

Garrett Whitlock (7-1) was credited with the victory. Aroldis Chapman got the final three outs for his 34th save and the 401st of his career.

Tolle, a hard-throwing 23-year-old left-hander, fanned Nick Loftin called, then got Bobby Witt Jr. and Jac Caglianone swinging in the first.

He went six scoreless innings, striking out seven while allowing four singles.

Noah Cameron gave up a run over six sharp innings.

Durbin belted Cameron's first pitch into the first row of seats above the Green Monster. Story's single came off Nate Pearson in the eighth.

Jensen's RBI single inside the first-base bag tied it.

The club announced Saturday that the finale's start time was pushed back 90 minutes due to the forecast of rain, which came and delayed the first pitch by 1 hour, 50 minutes.

Royals: RHP Michael Wacha (9-8, 3.25 ERA) is scheduled for the opener of a three-game series in Houston on Tuesday.

Red Sox: LHP Patrick Sandoval (1-5, 4.58) starts Tuesday in the series opener against Texas .

articles.title: How the Chargers lost to the Cardinals in Week 1's biggest upset
articles.summary: Here's a breakdown of how the Cardinals beat the Chargers.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the NFL season always seems to feature a surprising upset, and this year that win was courteous of the Arizona Cardinals .

While the Cardinals were expected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL this year, Arizona shocked the league by handling the Chargers in Los Angeles by a score of 26-14. Veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love helped get Mike LaFleur his first win as the team's head coach.

The Chargers , meanwhile, face a long week wondering what happened this week. Los Angeles has Super Bowl aspirations after adding Mike McDaniel as the new offensive coordinator, but the offense sputtered by scoring just 14 points.

Here's a breakdown of how the Cardinals beat the Chargers.

The Chargers disappointing loss to the Cardinals began on the very first drive, when Arizona marched down the field and scored to take a 7-0 lead. That 70-yard drive heavily featured rookie running back Jeremiyah Love, who punched it in for his first NFL touchdown.

Following that drive, the Chargers tied the game with a touchdown drive of their own, which was then followed by a Cardinals missed field goal. It seemed like Los Angeles had settled into the game, but that came to a halt when Omarion Hampton fumbled in Cardinals territory to squander a scoring chance.

On the ensuing drive, the Cardinals got a field goal to take a 10-7 lead midway through the second quarter.

Entering halftime, the Chargers were down just three points but had the benefit of receiving the kickoff in the second half. Unfortunately, they failed to do much with the ball as the offense go just 19 yards before punting away. The Cardinals would add a field goal on the next drive, extending the lead to six points.

Los Angeles did produce a touchdown drive to follow, taking a 14-13 lead midway through the third quarter. That score stuck for a while with both teams trading punts for the next few drives, but the play of the game came when Arizona blocked a Chargers punt to get the ball deep in Los Angeles Territory, turning that into a touchdown.

The Cardinals took the lead 20-14, putting the Chargers on the ropes. Finally, Justin Herbert through his lone interception of the day on a deep attempt, which essentially put the game away for the Cardinals as Arizona got a field goal on its next possession.

The 23-14 deficit proved to be too much for the Chargers to overcome with such little time left in the game. Arizona added another three points to cement the win at 26-14.

Los Angeles was discombobulated on offense though the entire game, and the Chargers special teams had a nightmare play that swung the game. The Cardinals, however, punched above their weight to get Mike LaFleur his first win as a head coach.

articles.title: Lions, happy to escape Week 1 with win, know they must 'clean this up'
articles.summary: "We will clean this up, and there's a lot to clean up," Lions coach Dan Campbell told his team in the postgame locker room.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions beat the New Orleans Saints at Ford Field on Sunday, Sept. 13, in an game that nearly ended with the hosts completely blowing a three-possession lead. The Lions , at one point up by 21 points, had to force an incompletion on New Orleans ' two-point attempt in overtime to secure the win .

"We did not play our cleanest," Lions coach Dan Campbell said in the postgame locker room, per video posted by the team . "But when we had to have it, all three phases — it's what we talked about last night, man. When we needed somebody to pull us back out of the water ... we did that in all three phases. ... That was the difference, man."

Detroit's near-collapse started with 8:49 remaining in the third frame, when Saints quarterback Tyler Shough scrambled right and found wide receiver Chris Olave deep down the sideline for a 47-yard catch. The Saints converted on third down twice and scored eight plays after Olave's explosive gain.

The Saints scored and then kicked a field goal, then scored again, to send the game to overtime, where Amon-Ra St. Brown scored what eventually proved to be the game-winning touchdown. St. Brown was one of three players to earn a game ball from Campbell after the game, along with linebacker Derrick Barnes and wide receiver Tay Martin .

"I don't give a f--- if it's one point or it's f------ 30 points, it's a f------ dub," Goff said in the locker room. "Use this s--- for momentum, boys. I promise you, we're gonna get on a roll, look back at Week 1, at that f------ two-point stop, as the s--- that got us there."

Barnes had an interception and a sack, and Martin tallied three tackles on special teams, including a couple of impressive reps on punt coverage.

"In the NFL, man, most games you play come down to the wire, and if you can just find a way to win," defensive end Aidan Hutchinson , who had two sacks in the opener, told reporters after the game. "There's a lot of talent in this league. Just win. That's the mantra."

Added cornerback D.J. Reed : "You take an ugly win or a pretty loss any day."

The Lions have a short week, set to travel to Buffalo to play the Bills and quarterback Josh Allen on Thursday, Sept. 17. It's the Bills' first game in Highmark Stadium, which opened in June.

"We're going to clean this up," Campbell told his team. "The biggest thing is right now, guys, is you find a way to get the win, it's Week 1, and then you clean the s--- up. Because it feels a hell of a lot better than the loss to have to clean it up.

"That's the thing, we found a way to win. We will clean this up, and there's a lot to clean up."

images.caption: Lions, happy to escape Week 1 with win, know they must 'clean this up'

articles.title: Top prospects Mitch Voit, Jonathan Santucci headline Mets' 2026 Player Development Awards
articles.summary: The Mets announced their 2026 Player Development Awards, honoring top prospects Mitch Voit as Player of the Year and Jonathan Santucci as Pitcher of the Year...
articles.body:
The Mets announced their 2026 Player Development Awards on Sunday with two top prospects headlining the honors.

They recognized infielder Mitch Voit as the Player of the Year and LHP Jonathan Santucci as the Pitcher of the Year.

Additionally among the player honors, outfielder Cleiner Ramirez was named the Mets ' DR Academy Player of the Year while RHP Abner Meza was named DR Academy Pitcher of the Year.

The recipients -- including field and gameplay coordinator David Adams (Minor League Staff Member of the Year), lead DSL hitting coach Bryce Wheary (DR Academy Staff Member of the Year) and senior scout Cesar Aranguren (Marlin McPhail Scout of the Year) -- are set to be honored in a pregame ceremony at Citi Field before Monday's 7:10 p.m. start on SNY against the Baltimore Orioles .

Voit, who turns 22 on Sept. 30, spent the 2026 season with High-A Brooklyn and Double-A Binghamton. In 29 games since his July 27 promotion, he slashed .347/.430/.517 with two home runs and 18 RBI.

Voit is No. 5 overall on the Mets' farm in SNY's latest ranking of the top 30 .

Santucci, 23, is the Mets' top pitching prospect on SNY's midseason list.

He earned his promotion from Binghamton to Triple-A Syracuse on July 28 after posting a 3.57 ERA in 19 games while striking out 120 and allowing an opposing batting average of .213. He has 37 strikeouts in seven starts over 29 innings with Syracuse.

articles.title: Tim Henman suggests what Ben Shelton needs to change after his US Open final defeat to Alexander Zverev
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev has continued his phenomenal season by beating Ben Shelton in the final of the US Open. Zverev is now a two-time Grand Slam...
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev has continued his phenomenal season by beating Ben Shelton in the final of the US Open.

Zverev is now a two-time Grand Slam champion, with the German having claimed his maiden title at this year's French Open.

The ATP number two, who also finished as runner-up at Wimbledon this summer, defeated Shelton 6-3, 7-6(7-2), 5-7, 6-2 in their highly anticipated US Open clash.

Zverev has since drawn praise from former British number one Tim Henman , who has more significantly suggested that the American should make a change to his game after this setback.

Ben Shelton told to make first serve more effective after US Open final loss

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, Henman said: "When I look at the first serve percentage of Shelton (71%), I would sacrifice some of that to say I am going to go bigger and harder.

"When he changes the pace and hits the 110mph kicker or slider, it's much easier to get back. When you are hitting serves at 140mph that is a nightmare to get back.

"That is where Zverev has continued to serve so well and so consistently and his average first serve speed is much faster than Shelton's.

"I think that's something Shelton has to go away and think about with his team to say how can he make that first serve more effective?"

It was certainly a battle between two big servers at Arthur Ashe Stadium, where the home favorite failed to come out on top, much to the disappointment of the majority of the fans.

Alexander Zverev vs Ben Shelton US Open final serving stats

Along with the title, Zverev has earned $5.5 million in prize money, while he's also extending his head-to-head record with the American to 6-0.

Adding further comment on the match-up, Henman said: "You look at the head-to-head record and it's 5-0. I think they have played four tiebreaks and he has won all of them.

"In the biggest moments he is coming up with the best tennis. 30-30 and deuce, the first eight times Zverev was at either score on serve he won those points.

"So Shelton did not have a break point in either of those sets, it is such a good platform for Zverev to build from."

The New York battle between the ATP superstars lasted three hours and 33 minutes, with Shelton certainly threatening a comeback on home soil.

But he ultimately fell short of a major challenge to his opponent, who is also now leading the Race to Turin rankings after collecting 2,000 points.

images.caption: Tim Henman suggests what Ben Shelton needs to change after his US Open final defeat to Alexander Zverev (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images)

articles.title: ‘Ultimate disrespect’ – Alexander Zverev’s Trinity Rodman moment draws strong reaction after US Open win
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev’s post-match banter with Trinity Rodman, the US soccer star and Ben Shelton’s girlfriend, caught the attention of fans after he defeated the...
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev's post-match banter with Trinity Rodman, the US soccer star and Ben Shelton's girlfriend, caught the attention of fans after he defeated the home favourite to win the second Grand Slam title of his career in the same year.

Zverev beat Shelton 6-3, 7-6 (7-2), 5-7, 6-2 in front of his home crowd to win his second Grand Slam title, becoming the second German after Boris Becker to win a US Open crown.

Alexander Zverev's Trinity Rodman banter gets fans talking

After the game was done and dusted, Zverev was on the mic thanking everyone before turning his attention to Rodman. The German asked her about her game before joking about her being Shelton's lucky charm, leading to a fun exchange between the two.

"Hey Trinity, I thought you have a game today, no? Well done to you as well. You're the lucky charm, so. Not today, but usually," Zverev joked.

ESPN shared a video of the moment on social media, and the exchange quickly prompted reactions from fans, with some viewing Zverev's comment as a particularly bold move after defeating Shelton in the final.

One fan wrote: "Beats him for the title, now trying to steal his gal. Cold."

Another fan simply called it: "The ultimate disrespect by Zverev."

A third fan took things further, writing: "Nah if I'm Ben I'm punching on Zverev. You ain't gonna embarrass me in the final and then be flirting with my girl like that. Oh hell nah."

Another person reacted: "Bro beat him and took a shot at his girl. Pure humiliation."

A fifth fan wrote: "Bro won the Grand Slam trophy and still found time to drop a stray comment. Coldest line of the entire tournament."

images.caption: Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP via Getty Images

articles.title: Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen dominates coverage in Week 1 victory
articles.summary: Riq Woolen saw four targets but allowed no catches or yards over 37 coverage snaps in his first start for the Philadelphia Eagles
articles.body:
Riq Woolen could not have provided a much stronger introduction to fans in the City of Brotherly Love during his first regular-season start with the Philadelphia Eagles . According to Ryan Fowler of NBC Sports Philadelphia , Woolen was targeted four times during Philadelphia's 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders . He did not allow a reception or a receiving yard across 37 coverage snaps.

Washington tested other areas of Philadelphia's secondary throughout the game, but Jayden Daniels found little success when directing the football toward Woolen. The Commanders quarterback completed 18 of 34 passes for 164 yards and two touchdowns. The performance illustrated why Philadelphia identified Woolen as an unquestioned starter after signing him to a one-year contract during the offseason.

At 6-foot-4, Woolen gives defensive coordinator Vic Fangio a rare combination of size, length, and recovery speed at outside cornerback. His physical traits let him disrupt receivers at the line of scrimmage while still able to recover when opponents test him vertically.

Philadelphia's secondary produced some uneven moments elsewhere. Cooper DeJean allowed a fourth-quarter touchdown to Stefon Diggs from the slot, while Washington moved within two points during the final minute.

Woolen remained steady throughout those difficulties. His coverage helped force Daniels to hold the football, move through his progressions, or target more favorable matchups on the opposite side.

One performance does not answer every question about Woolen's fit in Fangio's defense, but his debut represented an ideal beginning. If Woolen can consistently eliminate one side of the field, Philadelphia will have greater freedom to disguise coverages and direct safety help elsewhere.

images.caption: Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen dominates coverage in Week 1 victory
